solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Disorganised garçon omits gourmet

indicators.note: something disorganised is out of order, so the letters of the two words that follow are jumbled

explanation.surface: A muddled waiter leaves out dishes the food-lover ordered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disorganised' shuffles GARCON (the cedilla dropped) and OMITS. 'gourmet' is used as an adjective, as in 'a gourmet meal'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe fine eating and the art of good food, so they swap as adjectives.

clue.text: Very good graduate accepting position at last

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so the graduate word holds the other piece
at last points to the final letter of the word position

explanation.surface: A new graduate finally takes up a job and things are going very well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at last' takes N, the end of 'position', which 'accepting' places inside GRAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand is an informal British word of approval meaning excellent or fine.

clue.text: Holy trial Pius engineered

indicators.note: engineered means constructed or contrived, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A papal trial was rigged by Pope Pius.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engineered' rearranges TRIAL and PIUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiritual and holy are near synonyms for things relating to religion or the sacred.

clue.text: Fact that one's left land and buildings in America

indicators.note: with 's read as has, one has left means the letter for one has gone from the word for fact

parts.note: a fact is a reality, something that actually exists
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A statement that a single property has been abandoned somewhere in the US.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's left' reads as 'one has left': I leaves REALITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Realty is the US legal and real-estate term for property in land and buildings.

clue.text: Pinch new intellectual property

explanation.surface: Advice to steal a fresh patent or copyright.
explanation.definitionFit: To nip and to pinch both mean to squeeze sharply between finger and thumb.

clue.text: War club split by the newly-forged knife

indicators.note: a word split by another has that word put into a gap inside it

parts.note: a mace is a heavy club used as a weapon in medieval warfare

indicators.note: forged means hammered into a new shape, so the letters of the word the are reshaped

explanation.surface: A battle mace is cut through by a freshly made blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'newly-forged' rearranges the word 'the', and 'split by' sets the result inside the club; 'knife' fits a weapon surface but is only the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A machete is a broad heavy blade used for cutting through vegetation.

clue.text: With Reform even Clacton's getting better

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so the letters are rearranged into a new shape

parts.note: here the S of the possessive counts as a letter of the fodder

explanation.surface: Even the seaside town of Clacton is recovering now that Reform holds the seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reform' rearranges EVEN and CLACTONS. Clacton is an English seaside town in Essex, the seat of the Reform UK party's leader, so 'Reform' looks like the party.
explanation.definitionFit: A convalescent person is recovering after illness, which is to say improving in health.

clue.text: Derek could be running for bus

indicators.note: running suggests letters moving about loosely, so the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Derek may have to sprint to catch his bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' rearranges DEREKCOULDBE. A double-decker is the classic two-storey British bus.
explanation.definitionFit: A double-decker is a type of bus with two passenger levels, so it is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Instrument in Autocar in advert

indicators.note: in signals letters sitting within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A musical instrument shows up in an advertisement in a motoring magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to the letters inside 'Autocar in advert'. Autocar is a long-running British car magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocarina is a small egg-shaped wind instrument, an example of the class.

clue.text: Empty pie tin which can be used to make pie

definitions.text: which can be used to make pie

indicators.note: an empty word has lost its inside, leaving just its first and last letters

parts.note: a tin is a can, a metal food container

explanation.surface: A recipe telling you to clear out the pie dish for the next bake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empty' leaves P and E from 'pie'. 'pie' appears twice: once in the wordplay, once in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pecan nuts are the filling of the American pecan pie, so the nut fits the description.

clue.text: China trailing after terrible game

indicators.note: trailing after means coming behind, so the china word follows the other piece

parts.note: terrible means very bad
Minton is a famous English maker of fine china, so the name stands for china

explanation.surface: China lags behind after a dreadful performance in the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country, but the capital is just the start of the sentence: it is Minton porcelain.
explanation.definitionFit: Badminton is a racket sport played with a shuttlecock, an example of a game.

clue.text: Fruit tree close by in middle of bed outside court

indicators.note: outside means the first pieces wrap round the court abbreviation

parts.note: near means close by
taken as written

indicators.note: middle of takes the central letter of the word bed

explanation.surface: A fruit tree stands nearby, in the middle of a flower bed beyond the tennis court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of' takes the centre of 'bed'; 'outside' wraps the first pieces round the court abbreviation. The setter adds 'tree', which the blogger found unnecessary but the name covers the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A nectarine is a smooth-skinned peach, and the name covers the tree as well as its fruit.

clue.text: Exist over extended period of time

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word for exist is read backwards

parts.note: to exist is to be, and are is a form of be

explanation.surface: A remark about lingering on for a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns ARE round.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is a long, distinct period of history.

clue.text: Book flight

definitions.meaning: the second book of the Old Testament
a mass departure or escape of people

explanation.definitionFit: Exodus names both the Bible book and, generally, a mass departure such as the Israelites' flight.

clue.text: Casual worker not working?

parts.note: a machine that is off is not working
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: A labourer on temporary contract who is currently idle.
explanation.definitionFit: An offhand manner is casual or nonchalant, done without much care or thought.

clue.text: Finally see me following school programme

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the later pieces go behind the school abbreviation
finally takes the last letter of the word see

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asking to be seen at last after the school show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' takes E, the end of 'see'.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheme is a systematic plan of action, which is what a programme is.

clue.text: Plaster reportedly the cause of typing ooooooo … on keyboard?

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.words: the cause of typing ooooooo … on keyboard
parts.note: a run of repeated O letters happens when the O key is jammed down on the keyboard

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a keyboard producing endless O's and what might be to blame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' gives STUCK O, a jammed O key, whose sound matches the answer. The clue itself types seven O's.
explanation.definitionFit: Stucco is a fine plaster used to coat walls and make mouldings.

clue.text: Regularly tell off mischievous child

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the two words is taken

explanation.surface: Advice to scold a naughty youngster routinely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' takes the second, fourth and sixth letters of 'tell off'.
explanation.definitionFit: An elf is a sprite of folklore, and the word is used for an impish little child.

clue.text: Minced the garlic half-asleep

indicators.note: minced means chopped up finely, so the letters of the two words are cut up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A drowsy cook chops garlic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minced' rearranges THEGARLIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethargic means sluggish and drowsy, lacking energy, as one is when half-asleep.

clue.text: Blustering fellow full of hollow self-entitlement

indicators.note: full of means holding something, so the fellow word contains the other piece

parts.note: guy means a man or fellow

indicators.note: hollow means emptied inside, leaving just the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A loudmouth man puffed up with empty entitlement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hollow' leaves S and T from 'self-entitlement', which 'full of' puts inside GUY.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusty weather is windy and blustery, coming in sudden strong blasts.

clue.text: Leaf-eating creature destroyed a large oak

indicators.note: destroyed means broken apart, so these letters are pulled apart and rebuilt

explanation.surface: An animal that eats leaves has wrecked a big oak tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyed' rearranges A, L and OAK.
explanation.definitionFit: The koala of Australia lives almost entirely on eucalyptus leaves.

clue.text: Like small type of horse

parts.note: as means like, as in 'white as snow'

explanation.surface: A remark comparing something to a small breed of horse.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: an ass is a donkey, a member of the horse family rather than a true horse.
explanation.definitionFit: The ass, or donkey, is an equine animal closely related to the horse.

clue.text: Visibly embarrassed lad behind a lot of illegality

indicators.note: behind means coming after, so the lad word follows the other piece
a lot of means most but not all, so the last letter of the crime word is dropped

parts.note: crime is illegality, breaking the law
a son is a lad, a boy

explanation.surface: A young man blushing after being caught up in widespread wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' drops the final E from CRIME to leave CRIM.
explanation.definitionFit: To go crimson is to blush deep red, the visible sign of embarrassment.

clue.text: Repeat finding about dance music particularly

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters
disco is a style of dance music
very means particularly, as in very good

explanation.surface: A second discovery concerning a club sound, especially.
explanation.definitionFit: A rediscovery is finding something again, a second finding of what had been lost.
